sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No.
LAQ/ARB/NH-4(BET)/144/2010-11 dated 06.08.2021 pertaining to Sy. No. 41/2 measuring 218 Sq.
Meters of Bhattarahalli village.
.2.

The definite case of the petitioner is that property of the respondent No.1 measuring 218 Sq.
Meters in Sy. No. 41/2 of Bhattarahalli village has been acquired under Preliminary A.P.
No.19/2022 Notification issued by the respondent No. 2 under Section 3A(1) vide S.O. No.2117(E)
dated 18.12.2006 and Final Notification under Section 3D(1) and (2) vide S.O. No.1929(E) dated 14.11.2007.
The respondent No.3 has passed the award on 11.08.2008 and awarded a total compensation amount of Rs.15,25,202/- which has been received by the respondent No.1 under protest.

Subsequently, on 17.09.2019 the respondent No. 1 has filed the application for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.10,000/- per Sq. feet with interest @ 21% p.a., from the date of notification and 30% solatium.
Accordingly, the application is taken by the respondent No.2 for consideration.

.3. Thereafter, the Arbitrator hold an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ/ARB/NH-4 (BET),
144/143/142/82/2010- 11 dated 06.08.2021.
.4.

Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting aside the following:
:GROUNDS:
The petitioner claims that the impugned award passed by the respondent No. 2 is perverse, A.P. No.19/2022 patently illegal, capricious and goes against the fundamentals of Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

The respondent No.2 has grossly erred in not following the provisions of Secti9on 3-G(7)(a) of NH Act, the substantive law while passing the impugned award which is contrary to the provisions of Section 28 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

The respondent No.2 abruptly in the impugned Arbitral Award has relied upon the notification bearing No.
CVC/BUD/5/2006-07 dated 17.04.2007 without making any attempt to investigate the market value of the subject lands as on the date of Preliminary Notification and National Highways Authority Of India vs Premji Meghaji on 6 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17412316/

Meters under the aforesaid notification dated 17.04.2007 and the respondent No.2 has added 50% on the guidance value by holding that the subject lands are abutting NH.

Thereafter, the respondent No.2 has again added 25% on the guidance value and arrived at the rate of Rs. 14,598/- per Sq. Meters i.e., Rs. 8,342/- per Sq. Meters + Rs. 4,171/- (50% of Rs. 8,342/-) +
Rs. 2,085/- (25% of Rs. 8,342/-).
There are A.P. No.19/2022 manifest errors in the impugned Arbitral Award and consequently, the same is liable to be set aside under Section 34(2A) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
There are manifest errors in the impugned Arbitral Award and consequently the same is patently illegal.
Among other grounds, prayed to allow the petition.
.5. The respondent No. 1 to 3 though served with the notice, not chosen to appear before this Court to resist the petition and hence, they were placed exparte.
The entire records in LAQ/ARB/NH-4 (BET)/144/2010-11 secured from the Arbitrator.

.6. On the basis of above, the points for consideration are as under:
1) Whether the impugned award of the Arbitrator/SLAO is against law, fact, evidence and probabilities of the case and liable to be intervened by this Court?
2) What order or award?

A.P. No.19/2022 Ltd Vs. National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) (AIR 2019 SC 5041; (3) Som Dutt Builders Vs. State of Kerala (2009) 10 SCC 259 and (4) Copy of the judgment dated 11.03.2024 in A.P. No. 18/2022.

Perused the materials on record, on that basis my findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1 : In the affirmative Point No.2 : As per final order, for the following:
REASONS .8. POINT No.1:
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The respondent No.1 Sri. Premji Meghaji is an owner of the land in Sy. No.41/2 measuring to an extent of 218 Sq.
Meters of Bhattarahalli village and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-4 under Preliminary Notification dated 18.12.2006 and Final Notification dated 14.11.2007
is an admitted fact.

It is also an admitted and undisputed fact in this case that the respondent No.3/Special Land Acquisition and Competent Authority of National Highways Authority of India being a SLAO determined the compensation at Rs.6,996.34 per Sq. Meters for the acquired land.

sentences.text: .9. Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the respondent No. 1 Sri. Premji Meghaji filed an application before the respondent No. 2 claiming that he is entitled for compensation at the rate of Rs. 10,000/-per Sq. feet along with 25% interest from the date of notification and 30% solatium.

On basis of the said application, the respondent No. 2 hold an enquiry and passed order in LAQ /
ARB / NH-4 (BET) / 144 / 143 / 142 / 82 / 2010-11 dated 06.08.2021.

The respondent No. 2 has held that the guidance value of NA lands situated at Bhattarahalli village was Rs. 775/- per Sq. feet i.e., Rs. 8,342/- per Sq. Meters and added 50% on the guidance value by holding that the subject lands are abutting National Highway.

The respondent No. 2 again added 25% on the guidance value and arrived at the rate of Rs.14,598/-
per Sq. Meters plus Rs. 4,171 (50% of Rs. 8,342/-) + Rs. 2,085 (25% of Rs. 8,342).
The respondent No. 2 in its order enhanced the compensated at Rs.14598/- per Sq. Meters by adding Rs.7602/- to the compensation decided by the respondent No. 3 i.e., Rs.6,996/-.
. The said enhancement has been challenged by the petitioner in this petition.

The grievance of the petitioner is that the respondent No. 2 without considering the relevant provisions of NHA Act and also without considering the guidance value or market value of the property as on the date of Preliminary Notification enhanced the compensation by relying on the guidance value of the year 2007-08 published vide notification bearing No.CVC/BUD/5/2006-07 dated 17.04.2007 which came to effect from 19.04.2007 and the said document is not part of arbitration proceedings.
The petitioner also claimed that the Preliminary Notification dated 18.12.2006.
As such, the respondent No. 2 ought to have considered the market value of the land of the year 2006 and not of the year 2007.
As the aforesaid notification relied by the Arbitrator came to effect from 2007 i.e., after lapse of more than 4 months from the date of publication of Preliminary Notification.
Accordingly claimed that the said enhancement cannot be accepted.
It is true that as per the NH Act, the market value of the land as on the date of Preliminary Notification has to be considered.
The petitioner also claimed that whatever the document relied by the respondent No. 2 for enhancing the compensation is not brought to the notice of the petitioner before passing the award/judgment.
Accordingly, claimed that such award is liable to be set aside as per Section 24 of National Highways Authority Act.
In this context, the petitioner relied on the decision reported in (2019) 15 SCC 131 in a case of Ssangyong Engineering and Construction Company Limited Vs. National Highways Authority of India.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is true that in the said decision, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that whatever the document relied by the Arbitrator shall be brought to the notice of the parties, so that the parties can make submission or give a rebuttal evidence about such documents.
However, in the case on hand, such notification is not found in the record received from the Arbitrator.
In the case on hand, the Arbitrator has enhanced compensation to tune of 75%.
Of course there is some reason for enhancement of 50%, but there is no reasoning for enhancement of 25% of the compensation amount.

It is simply stated that 25% compensation has been enhanced National Highways Authority Of India vs Premji Meghaji on 6 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17412316/
4 by using the discretion.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is well settled principle of law that discretion must be used judiciously and not arbitrarily.

What A.P. No.19/2022 ever the enhancement has been granted by the Arbitrator,
certainly effect the State or State Exchequer.
Hence, Arbitrator shall give reasons for enhancement of the compensation.
As already stated above, the Arbitrator / respondent No. 2 has not given any explanation for enhancement of 25% in addition to 50%.
Hence such enhancement cannot be accepted.

.12. In the case on hand, the respondent No.1 claimed that proper award has been passed and no such case has been made out by the petitioner to intervene with the award passed by the respondent No. 2.

When the respondent No. 2 claimed that the respondent No. 2 has passed the order or order is not in accordance with law, then it is for the respondent No. 1 to show that the order passed by the respondent No. 2 is in accordance with law and said order has been passed by following all procedure contemplated under law.

.13. In the case on hand, though the respondent No.1 served with the notice not chosen to appear before the court to resist the case of the petition case or to support the award passed by the respondent No. 2.
Absolutely no material placed before the court to disbelieve the petition case or to substantiate the award A.P. No.19/2022 passed by the respondent No. 2.
Hence, this Court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to intervene with the award passed by the Arbitrator and the award is liable to be set aside.
Accordingly, the point No. 1 is held in the affirmative.
.14. Point No.2: In view of my above finding, I proceed to pass the following.
ORDER Petition is allowed.

Consequently, the award passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No. 2 in case No.
LAQ/ARB/NH-4(BET)/144/2010-11 dated 06.08.2021 pertaining to Sy. No. 41/2 measuring 218 Sq.
Meters of Bhattarahalli village is set aside with a liberty to the parties to pursue their remedy in accordance with law.
Office is directed to send back the Lower Court Records.
